deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's axiomatic sketch of a category Esp_Mo of 'espaces modérés' (tame spaces). The surrounding pages build the theory from a list of axioms (M1)…(M10) on a class of subsets of R and R^n, modelled on semialgebraic sets. The page makes three points.

(1) Opening sentence (hard to read). It recalls that there is a notion of a map X → Y between tame spaces being 'modérée au voisinage d'un point' (tame near a point).

(2) Proposition: a map from a tame space X into a tame (possibly 'ind-modéré') space Y is tame if and only if it is tame near every point. In modern terms, tameness of maps is a local property.

(3) Consequences.
- Tame maps X → Y form the sections of a sheaf on X, the sheaf of tame maps.
- The tame structure of X is determined by the set of tame functions X → R. Grothendieck says this already follows from the weak axiom set (M1)_0, (M2), (M3), (M4).
- Hence the structure is also determined by the sheaf of germs of tame functions.

In modern language, this presents a tame space as a topological space carrying a subsheaf of the sheaf of continuous R-valued functions: a 'space with functions', or an R-locally-ringed space. It also shows Esp_Mo embeds fully faithfully into such sheaf-structured spaces.

The purpose is to prepare the next page. There Grothendieck defines 'espaces localement modérés' by gluing (separated spaces in which every point has a tame neighbourhood) and asks that compact parts be exactly those contained in a tame part. Locality of tame maps, and the sheaf description, are what make such gluing meaningful.
errors: The Proposition is true only if tame spaces are 'compact-like', so that a tame space is covered by finitely many tame neighbourhoods and tame maps glue along finite covers.

For non-compact definable/semialgebraic spaces the statement fails. Example: on R, a piecewise-linear zigzag with infinitely many corners is locally semialgebraic but not semialgebraic. This is exactly the distinction between semialgebraic and locally semialgebraic spaces.

The next page treats R^n as merely 'localement modéré' and links compact parts to tame parts. This suggests Grothendieck's tame spaces are implicitly bounded or compact-type objects, in which case the Proposition is correct.
Even in that case, the page gives no proof. It needs an unstated axiom that tame maps glue along finite (open or closed) tame covers.

ideas.what: Tameness of maps is local: a map is tame iff it is tame near each point (for compact-type tame spaces).
ideas.modern_name: Locality of definable / semialgebraic maps on definably compact spaces; gluing of definable maps along finite covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs–Knebusch (semialgebraic topology, 1981–85); van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal Structures (1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only calls for a 'topologie modérée'; no such proposition appears there

ideas.what: Tame maps X→Y form a sheaf; the tame structure is determined by the sheaf of germs of tame R-valued functions.
ideas.modern_name: Semialgebraic / definable spaces as locally ringed spaces (sheaf of continuous semialgebraic/definable functions); spaces with functions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs–Knebusch (semialgebraic spaces as ringed spaces, ~1981; Locally Semialgebraic Spaces, LNM 1173, 1985); Brumfiel; Coste–Roy

ideas.what: The tame structure is recoverable from tame functions to R alone, already under a minimal axiom set ((M1)_0, (M2)–(M4)).
ideas.modern_name: Definable structure determined by definable real-valued functions (embedding of definable spaces into R-spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in o-minimal geometry / real algebraic geometry

missed.claim: In an axiomatic tame-topology framework predating o-minimality (dated from 1973/1978 onward), Grothendieck states that tame maps form a sheaf and that the tame structure is determined by the sheaf of germs of tame functions. He also notes that this needs only a small fragment of his axioms. This anticipates the ringed-space treatment of semialgebraic spaces by Delfs–Knebusch, and next page's tame vs locally tame distinction mirrors their semialgebraic vs locally semialgebraic.
missed.quote: Donc les applications modérées de X dans Y forment les sections d'un faisceau ... La structure modérée de X est connue quand on connait l'ens. des applications modérées de X dans R (cela ressort dans le contexte présent axiomatique, avec (M1)_0 (M2) (M3) (M4) seulement)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that Grothendieck's unpublished 'topologie modérée' was organised sheaf-theoretically, in parallel with, and possibly earlier than, the real-algebraic-geometry literature. The mathematics itself is standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard: locality of tame maps and the sheaf of tame functions are routine in semialgebraic/o-minimal geometry. The only interest is historical, as an early axiomatic and sheaf-theoretic framing by Grothendieck, which mirrors Delfs–Knebusch.
transcription_corrections: First line: the word inserted above the caret is 'dans'. The following 'C'[?]' is unclear; the sentence may read 'On sait dans quel cas ... la notion d'application X → Y entre espaces modérés qui est modérée au voisinage d'un pt'. The words 'modérée au voisinage d'un pt' are underlined in the manuscript.
In the Prop, the target space is probably 'un espace ind-modéré' rather than 'un espace modéré[?]'; the handwriting shows a prefix before 'modéré'.
The end of the first paragraph reads more like 'et on trouve...' or 'et en termes...' than 'et en tous[?]'.
'(M1)_0 s' is probably '(M1)_0' followed by a stray mark; the closing parenthesis comes after 'seulement'.
